Many couples believe that having a regular menstrual cycle guarantees regular ovulation. However, regular periods don't always mean regular ovulation, and hidden fertility issues can still exist behind the scenes.

• Regular periods don't guarantee regular ovulation.

Don't guess when it comes to your reproductive health. Get a complete fertility evaluation.

Uterine fibroids are benign, non-cancerous growths that develop within or around the muscular walls of the uterus. While many women with fibroids conceive without medical intervention, certain types can influence fertility.

Depending on their size, number, and location, fibroids can:
• Alter the shape of the uterine cavity, impacting embryo implantation.
• Restrict optimal blood circulation to the uterine lining.
• Obstruct the fallopian tubes.

At Embrion IVF Center, we assess each case individually. If a fibroid is affecting your fertility, modern, minimally invasive management can restore optimal uterine health before starting treatment.

If you have faced repeated embryo implantation failure despite transferring high-quality embryos, immune factors within the reproductive tract may be a contributing factor worth investigating.

Natural Killer (NK) cells are a standard, protective component of the body's immune system. However, an imbalance of these cells within the uterine lining can sometimes affect how the body responds to an embryo, impacting its ability to implant safely.

Through advanced reproductive immunological testing, our laboratory can evaluate these cell levels and implement targeted therapeutic options to foster a more receptive environment.

Not every normal delivery progresses smoothly till the end. In some cases, labour advances well but the baby does not deliver despite good contractions. When the cervix is fully open and the baby’s head is already low, vacuum assisted delivery may be used to help complete the birth safely. This is a form of assisted delivery used only under specific conditions.

During vacuum delivery, a suction cup is attached to the baby’s head and gentle assistance is given while the mother pushes with contractions. This helps reduce prolonged strain during the second stage of labour and allows timely delivery when support is needed.

At Pradnya Maternity IVF and Multispeciality Hospital in Mulund, Dr Pradnya Randive manages labour and delivery with careful assessment at every stage. The focus is on safe normal delivery, early identification of delivery delays, and using assisted methods only when they are medically appropriate for the mother and baby.

Heavy Periods & Painful Periods Should Not Be Ignored

Many women experience heavy bleeding during periods, severe cramps, or both, and assume it is normal. However, when periods last more than 7 days, involve passing large clots, or require frequent pad changes, this condition is called menorrhagia. When periods are extremely painful and interfere with daily activities, it is known as dysmenorrhea.

According to Dr. Pradnya Randive, Obstetrician Gynaecologist and Fertility Specialist at Pradnya Maternity IVF & Multispeciality Hospital, Mulund, these symptoms often have underlying medical causes such as fibroids, endometriosis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), or thyroid-related problems. Ignoring them can lead to anaemia, fertility issues, and long-term health complications.

Early consultation with a gynaecologist helps identify the cause through basic evaluations such as blood tests and pelvic sonography, allowing timely and effective treatment. Not all heavy or painful periods require surgery, but they do require proper medical assessment.

At Pradnya Maternity IVF & Multispeciality Hospital, women receive personalised care for menstrual problems, pregnancy, and normal delivery, with a focus on accurate diagnosis and safe treatment.

If you are facing heavy bleeding, painful periods, or irregular cycles, consult a gynaecologist early and avoid self-medication.
